title: Effects of black soldier fly replacing fish meal on growth performance, serum parameters, and intestinal microbiota of weaned piglets
content:
Lay Summary
Fish meal (FM), a critical protein source in piglet diets, faces supply constraints and rising costs due to overfishing. The black soldier fly (BSF) has emerged as a promising sustainable alternative owing to its high nutrient density, efficiency in upcycling organic waste, and superior feed conversion. This study systematically evaluated the effects of replacing FM with varying levels of BSF on growth performance, nutrient utilization, serum parameters, intestinal microbiota, and metabolites of weaned piglets. The results indicate that partial or complete replacement of FM with BSF had no adverse effects on growth performance or nutrient digestibility. Moreover, BSF substitution increased short-chain fatty acid levels and decreased biogenic amine levels by altering the intestinal microbiota composition. These changes in microbial fermentation products may benefit immune responses and antioxidant functions of piglets. Our findings support BSF as a sustainable protein source that can improve the health status of weaned piglets.
